ov: Venomous snakes that rear up and spread a hood when threatened. Most belong to the genus Naja; the king cobra, the longest venomous snake, isn’t a true cobra despite its name.

why.et: King cobras are poached and sold as bushmeat, turned into snake leather and used in traditional Chinese medicine.

len: King cobra: usually 3.18–4 m; record 5.85 m
wt: Up to about 10 kg (king cobra, males)
rg: True cobras: Africa and Asia. King cobra: India through Southeast Asia to southern China.
df: The king cobra hunts mainly other snakes, including other king cobras.
fx: The king cobra can deliver 400–600 mg of venom in a single bite.
notes: Group entry (alias “king cobra”). The existing fact is confirmed: the king cobra is "the only ophidian that constructs an above-ground nest for its eggs". Sizes are for the king cobra; true cobras are smaller. The king cobra is IUCN Vulnerable, but I left iu out because this entry covers all cobras.
